note: A 2024 multicenter cohort study confirmed distinct genotype-phenotype neuroradiological correlations between biallelic loss-of-function variants (periatrial volume loss resembling PVL) and biallelic cysteine missense variants (CADASIL-like deep white matter lesions without marked volume loss).

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants lead to periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants present with deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

numbers.metric: patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in NOTCH3 cause an autosomal recessive disorder marked by early-onset neurological signs and periventricular white matter abnormalities, distinct from classic CADASIL.

source.title: A novel homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant in a Moroccan patient: expanding the spectrum beyond CADASIL
source.quote: Emerging evidence shows that biallelic loss-of-function variants, unlike the gain-of-function variants underlying CADASIL, define a distinct autosomal recessive leukodystrophy characterized by early-onset pyramidal signs, epilepsy, and white matter abnormalities, thereby expanding the phenotypic and molecular spectrum of NOTCH3-related disorders.
